They're still technically on the board but are dead players. This leaves it as a two-player match between me and GPT, and I need to assess my position going forward.

I'm sitting at $1,391 cash with my light-blue monopoly fully developed (4 houses each on Oriental, Vermont, and Connecticut generating $400-450 per landing). I've also mortgaged Tennessee, Kentucky, Illinois, and B&O to preserve cash. GPT has $547 and a scattered portfolio—hotels on the browns, 4 houses on his magenta and orange properties, and partial development on the greens, but most of his dark properties are mortgaged.

The critical constraint is that the bank has zero houses remaining. My famine strategy of holding 12 houses has been working perfectly to lock GPT out of further development, and with the bank depleted, he can't build anything anyway. If I convert my houses to hotels, I'd return those houses to the bank and give him the opportunity to build on his greens, which would be a strategic mistake. The winning play is to maintain the famine, hold my position, and let my lethal light-blue rents grind him down—he's only two bad rolls away from bankruptcy at his current cash level. I should just end my turn and stick with this dominant position.
